result: The manuscript establishes background knowledge about Obps: they are highly abundant in insect antennae, widely divergent in sequence but conserved in structure, bind odorants in vitro, are found in sensillar lymph, and have been believed essential for transporting hydrophobic odorants through aqueous lymph for over 30 years.
evaluation: These claims represent well-established prior knowledge supported by multiple citations (C1, C2, C20-C29). The claims are consistent with the literature and provide necessary context for the study. No experimental validation is required as these are literature-based background claims.

result: The authors previously constructed an Obp-to-sensillum map showing that 10 Obps are expressed at much higher levels than others in the antenna, with different basiconic sensilla containing different subsets of four abundant Obps (Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a, Obp83b).
evaluation: These claims describe prior work by the authors (Larter et al., 2016) that is well-documented and illustrated in Figure 1E. The map provides the foundation for the current study's experimental design and is supported by published data.

result: Previous work showed that deletion of Obp28a from the ab8 sensillum, which contains only this single abundant Obp, resulted in retained or enhanced olfactory responses to various odorants, indicating Obp28a is not essential for robust olfactory response in ab8.
evaluation: These claims summarize the authors' previous findings (Larter et al., 2016) that motivated the current study. The prior work is properly cited and provides critical context, though C39 notes ab8 may be exceptional since Obp28a is expressed in all basiconic sensilla.

result: The authors generated CRISPR-Cas9 deletions of Obp19a, Obp28a, and Obp83a/b genes, outcrossed them for five generations to minimize genetic background effects, verified deletions by PCR multiple times, and tested mutant and control flies in parallel using standardized electrophysiology protocols.
evaluation: The experimental methodology is clearly described with appropriate controls (C40-C41, C122). The genetic deletions are substantial (91% of Obp19a, 85% of Obp83b, C117, C120) and properly verified. The parallel testing design and outcrossing strategy address potential confounds. Methods are reproducible and rigorous.

result: Morphological examination of approximately 1000 basiconic sensilla from ~20 mutant flies lacking all four abundant Obps revealed no gross defects in size, morphology, or position.
evaluation: This finding is supported by scanning electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 (C42). The sample size is substantial (C131) and the morphological analysis was not performed in the previous study, making this a valuable addition.

result: All six tested sensillum types (ab1-ab6) responded robustly to diverse odorants when their abundant Obps were deleted. Response magnitudes were indistinguishable from controls in all cases, with no olfactory response diminished by Obp absence.
evaluation: This major finding is supported by extensive electrophysiological data in Figure 2A-F (C43-C48). The claims are consistent across multiple sensillum types, odorant-ORN combinations, and concentrations. Statistical analysis shows no significant differences (p>0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). The conclusion that none of the tested Obps are essential for robust responses (C72-C75) is well-supported.

result: The study tested 37 odorants representing diverse chemical classes with hydrophobicity ranging over five orders of magnitude (logP -1.33 to 4.28), including four more hydrophobic than any previously tested. All 85 odorant-ORN combinations showed normal responses across 12 ORNs with varying tuning breadth.
evaluation: The breadth of testing is well-documented (C77, C132-C135) with data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2. The inclusion of highly hydrophobic odorants (C49, C78) directly addresses whether Obps are essential for transporting hydrophobic compounds. The 73 additional odorant-ORN combinations (C50) all showed normal responses, strengthening the conclusion.

result: Spontaneous activity levels of all 12 neurons tested were normal in the absence of abundant Obps (p>0.05 in all cases, Mann-Whitney U test, n=10).
evaluation: This finding is supported by statistical analysis with appropriate sample size (n=10) and statistical test. The normal spontaneous activity indicates that Obp deletion does not grossly impair neuronal function, supporting the specificity of the findings.

result: ORNs in ab3 sensilla lacking all four abundant Obps responded robustly to both intermittent (repeated 0.5s pulses) and prolonged (5s) odor stimuli, with response dynamics comparable to controls throughout rising, peak, and falling phases for multiple odorants.
evaluation: This result is supported by detailed electrophysiological recordings and peri-stimulus time histograms in Figure 3 (C53-C58). The analysis of response dynamics addresses whether Obps play temporal roles in odorant transport or removal. Testing both intermittent and prolonged stimuli (C52, C59, C79) strengthens the conclusion that Obps are not essential for diverse temporal patterns.

result: The ab4 sensillum mutant lacking Obp19a and Obp28a showed significantly stronger physiological responses to a linoleic acid sample than controls across multiple concentrations, consistent with previous findings in ab8.
evaluation: This finding is supported by dose-response data in Figure 4A showing statistically significant increases (p<0.05, p<0.01) across multiple dilutions (C63, C64). The result is consistent with prior work on ab8 (C100, C102) and demonstrates that some Obps can modulate rather than enable olfactory responses.

result: The Obp mutant showed a shifted oviposition dose-response curve to linoleic acid sample, with lower thresholds for both attraction and aversion compared to controls, demonstrating that increased physiological response translates to altered behavioral response.
evaluation: This behavioral result is supported by oviposition preference data in Figure 4C (C65-C68). The shift in the entire dose-response relationship (C68) and the correspondence between physiological and behavioral changes (C81, C115) provide strong evidence that Obps can modulate both sensory and behavioral responses. This is a novel extension to the behavioral level.

result: After experiments were completed, evidence emerged that physiological responses of ab4A to long chain hydrophobic compounds may arise from trace impurities in commercial preparations rather than the compounds themselves.
evaluation: This claim acknowledges a potential confound identified by Schorkopf et al. (2018) after the current experiments were conducted. While this raises questions about the identity of the actual stimulus, the authors appropriately refer to 'linoleic acid sample' rather than pure linoleic acid. The key finding—that Obp deletion affects responses—remains valid regardless of the precise chemical identity.

result: The results support a model in which many sensilla can respond to odorants without Obps, many Obps are not essential for olfactory response, but some Obps can modulate olfactory physiology and behavior.
evaluation: This interpretive model (C6-C8, C71, C110, C112, C114) is well-supported by the comprehensive data showing robust responses in Obp mutants (Figures 2-3) combined with the modulatory effects observed in ab4 (Figure 4). The model appropriately distinguishes between essential and modulatory roles, reconciling the lack of deficits in most cases with the enhanced responses in specific contexts.

result: The authors acknowledge the formal possibility that Obp loss initially caused deficits that were suppressed during genetic crosses, but argue this is unlikely given the requirement for complete suppression across all sensilla and mutants within limited generations.
evaluation: This is a reasonable acknowledgment of a formal possibility (C83) with appropriate logical argumentation against it (C84). The authors correctly note that complete suppression across all tested conditions would be unlikely. The five-generation outcrossing and parallel testing design (C40, C122) help address this concern.

result: The authors acknowledge that low-abundance Obps (expressed 2-3 orders of magnitude lower than the deleted Obps) could theoretically provide redundant function, though this would require complete compensation across all sensilla.
evaluation: This formal possibility (C85) is appropriately acknowledged, and the expression data (C86) is cited from prior work. However, the authors correctly note that complete functional compensation by such low-abundance proteins across all contexts would be remarkable. This remains a limitation that cannot be definitively excluded without testing all Obps.

result: The authors acknowledge their analysis is not exhaustive, testing at most three concentrations per odorant-ORN combination, and that more extensive dose-response analysis or different stimulus durations might reveal phenotypes.
evaluation: This is an appropriate and honest acknowledgment of study limitations (C87-C90). While the breadth of testing is impressive (37 odorants, 85 combinations), the depth at each combination is limited. The speculation about what additional testing might reveal (C89, C90) is reasonable and does not undermine the main findings.

result: The interpretation that Obps are not universally required for odorant transport is consistent with recent findings that Obps function in non-olfactory processes (hematopoiesis, wound-healing, humidity detection) and are expressed outside the olfactory system.
evaluation: These claims appropriately contextualize the findings within recent literature (C92-C94) showing diverse Obp functions. The citations are relevant and support the interpretation (C91). The speculation that antennal Obps might have non-olfactory roles (C111) is reasonable given the evidence.

result: Genomic analyses reveal dramatic expansions of odorant receptor genes in some insects (e.g., ants with ~400 Ors but only 13-16 Obps), arguing against classic models requiring matched Obp-receptor pairs.
evaluation: These comparative genomic observations (C95-C98) are well-supported by citations and provide compelling evidence against models requiring one-to-one Obp-receptor matching (C99). The major numerical imbalances in ants are particularly striking and support the authors' interpretation.

result: Previous work suggested Obps might function in molecular gain control based on enhanced responses to some odorants in ab8 mutants. The current linoleic acid results are consistent with a model where Obps bind odorants and reduce the concentration reaching ORNs.
evaluation: The gain control hypothesis (C101) and the concentration reduction model (C107) are reasonable interpretations of the enhanced response phenotypes, but remain speculative. The data show that Obp deletion increases responses in specific contexts, but the mechanism is not directly tested. Alternative explanations are not fully explored.

result: A recent study found robust responses when Obp83a/b were deleted from trichoid and intermediate sensilla, though three of ten neurons showed slow deactivation kinetics. The authors propose Obps remove odorants after receptor activation.
evaluation: These claims accurately summarize findings from Scheuermann and Smith (2019) with appropriate citations (C104-C106). The observation that abundant protein removal has limited effects (C108) is a valid interpretation shared between studies, though the deactivation phenotype in the other study suggests some functional role.

result: The study extends previous analysis from one to seven basiconic sensilla, one to four Obps (which are highly divergent in sequence, e.g., Obp83a shows only 15.6-21.3% identity to other tested Obps), and 12 to 37 odorants.
evaluation: The scope expansion (C113) is clearly documented and represents a substantial advance over prior work. The sequence divergence data (C76) supports the conclusion that functionally diverse Obps were tested, strengthening the generalizability of findings.

result: The study focused on basiconic sensilla because detailed Obp-to-sensillum maps were available. Oviposition assays used standardized conditions with 10 females per dish for 20-24 hours, excluding dishes with fewer than 10 eggs.
evaluation: The rationale for focusing on basiconic sensilla (C103) is sound given the available mapping data. The oviposition methodology (C124-C126) is clearly described with appropriate exclusion criteria. The experimental design is reasonable and reproducible.

result: The behavioral effect with linoleic acid sample is consistent with the physiological effect and may have significant ecological relevance for the animal in natural contexts.
evaluation: While the consistency between physiological and behavioral effects is well-demonstrated (supported by Figure 4), the speculation about ecological significance (C109) is not directly tested. The natural relevance depends on whether flies encounter similar stimuli in nature and whether the Obp modulation affects fitness, which are not addressed.
